works_well.theme: Signing up helpers for shifts, tasks and meals
works_well.what_it_means: People use it so helpers can claim shifts or tasks and see who signed up.

quotes.quote: Great to have on-the-go when you need to check who has signed up for different tasks.
Lotsa Helping Hands (great for meal trains, not for meds/money)

does_not_work_well.what_it_means: The app shows a blank screen or crashes, stopping people from signing up or adding events.

quotes.quote: I NEED to sign up for shifts next week but just cannot get the app to let me do it.
Not useful or trustworthy if there are glitches like this.

setup_and_ease_of_use.what_it_means: Two of three reviewers could not complete simple steps because the app froze, crashed or went blank.

quotes.quote: I Go into the app and I can’t get anything to show up. It just is a blank screen.
every time it asks if I want to add to my calendar and I say yes, it crashes.

single_mentions.point: Used by friends of a family with a child in cancer treatment to sign up for help shifts; website also glitchy
Long-time user says the mobile app is as good as or easier than the website
iPhone only, no iPad app; tester did not trust it after crashes
Seen as good for meal trains but not for medications or money; family still runs care through a group chat, an unused shared Notes app and photos of pill bottles

reader_notes: Very thin evidence: 4 items. Two of the three app reviews are from 2013, so they describe an old app. The Reddit writer is a caregiver but says they are thinking about building their own product, and their Lotsa comment is a short judgment, not a description of using it. The two dropped Reddit posts matched only on the word 'lotsa' (as in 'lotsa room') or did not mention the product at all.
